cards.title: Define a function
cards.body: `def` creates a function: a named block of code that runs whenever you call it by name. The body is indented.

hi.title: Function define karo
hi.body: `def` ek function banata hai: code ka ek naam wala block jo jab bhi uska naam call karo, chalta hai. Body indented hoti hai.

cards.title: Parameters and return
cards.body: Values go in through parameters in the brackets. `return` sends a result back to whoever called the function.
cards.code:
def double(n):
    return n * 2


print(double(5))
print(double(21))

hi.title: Parameters aur return
hi.body: Values brackets ke andar parameters se andar aati hain. `return` result ko wapas usko bhejta hai jisne function call kiya.

cards.title: return is not print
cards.body: `print` only shows a value. `return` hands it back, so the caller can keep using it, for example in more maths.
cards.code:
def add_one(n):
    return n + 1


x = add_one(4) * 10
print(x)

hi.title: return, print nahi hai
hi.body: `print` value sirf dikhata hai. `return` use wapas deta hai, taaki call karne wala use aage use kar sake, jaise aur maths mein.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print 11, but prints 10 and then crashes with a `TypeError`. Which line is wrong?
cards.code:
def double(n):
    print(n * 2)

result = double(5) + 1
print(result)

bug.fix: `print` only shows the value, so `double` gives back `None`. Line 2 should be `return n * 2`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse 11 print karna chahiye, par yeh 10 print karta hai aur phir `TypeError` dekar crash hota hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: `print` sirf value dikhata hai, isliye `double` wapas `None` deta hai. Line 2 `return n * 2` honi chahiye.
